research_period: Pitti Bimbo 103, Florence, 24-25 June 2026; Playtime Paris, 28-30 June 2026; analysis July to November 2026
markets: Europe-led kidswear trade fairs; premium and mid-market childrenswear, newborn to teen
title: SS27 Kids' Trim Market Strategy
summary: In a slowing childrenswear market, use trims to add value to fewer, longer-lasting pieces; avoid fragile decoration that shortens a garment's life.

sections.heading: The market context
sections.body: In Italy, childrenswear exports fell 9.3% and domestic sales 2.6% in 2025, according to Confindustria Moda data reported by Fortune Italia; families are focused on sustainability and well-being, and the sector is moving toward functionality, material quality and durability<sup>[1]</sup>. Fashion overall is expected to remain in low single-digit growth in 2027<sup>[2]</sup>.

sections.heading: Build, test, sell through
sections.body:
| Action | Trims |
|---|---|
| Build | Embroidery, appliqué, sailor collars and tape |
| Test | Shell and bead decoration (older kids only), sparkle for party |
| Sell through | Fragile glued decoration |

design_implications:
- Choose trims that survive repeated washing and hand-me-downs.
- Safety: no drawstrings or long cords at the hood, neck or waist of young children's clothing, in line with EN 14682; test the attachment strength of buttons, beads, shells and other decorations, and keep small detachable parts off baby and toddler pieces.
commercial_implications: - Durable trims support resale and hand-me-down value, which parents increasingly consider.
